content_blocks.label: lead_paragraph
content_blocks.text: Governor Robert Johnson has unveiled a proposal to raise the state’s minimum wage from $10.50 to $15 per hour over the next three years, aiming to alleviate poverty and boost consumer spending.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_1
content_blocks.text: The governor’s plan includes a gradual increase in wages, with the first hike occurring six months after the bill is signed into law. He argues that this will help lift thousands out of poverty and stimulate economic growth.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_2
content_blocks.text: Opponents contend that such a significant increase could lead to job losses in low-wage sectors, particularly in small businesses. They also worry about inflationary pressures and higher prices for consumers.

content_blocks.label: body_paragraph_3
content_blocks.text: Advocates for workers’ rights praise the governor’s initiative, saying it will provide much-needed relief to those struggling to make ends meet.

content_blocks.label: pull_quote
content_blocks.text: "No one who works full-time should live in poverty. This is a fair and necessary step forward." - Governor Robert Johnson
